rationale: B wins because "Perplexity now earns a fee when you buy what it recommends" finds the trust/accountability story A leaves sitting on the table. A has real work in "Does 'hundreds of millions of queries' add up to a real shopping channel for Perplexity?", but it also splits one publisher story into two envelopes and oversells "the same ones it's now offering to pay." B is cleaner: publishers, merchants, investors, users.
gaps_in_A: "The publishers threatening Perplexity with lawsuits are the same ones it's now offering to pay" overstates the facts; the update says publishers criticized and legally threatened Perplexity, not that those same publishers are eligible, enrolled, or being paid.

"Distinct from the defensive-comment angle" is too tidy. The legal-conflict and undisclosed-payout angles are probably one media-business story unless A can produce a named publisher reaction or real payout math.

"Perplexity's new revenue streams are the receipts its last valuation is betting on" sells an investor thesis before proving one. A knows this, because it later asks whether tying the revenue streams to the valuation would be speculation.
A misses the obvious user-trust hook inside "earning a referral fee": whether paid commerce incentives affect rankings, labels, or recommendations.
gaps_in_B: "This is the company's first structural answer to that fight" invents chronology. The update gives a program launch, not proof it is the first answer to publisher conflict.
"takes a referral fee on every sale" is too absolute. The facts say Perplexity earns a referral fee from in-app purchases, not that every sale or every merchant relationship works that way.
"The launch is the first concrete monetization signal since the raise" is unsupported. The update says there was a recent raise, not that no other monetization signals existed.

"A self-reported, uncontextualized query count with undisclosed payouts gives a data reporter nothing to pull" throws away a usable retail-channel math question too quickly; commercial-query share and conversion rate would make that angle reportable.
